note: Rewritten from the original description by Light (1930); the original is in English and describes the alate, the soldier and large and small workers. Type locality: Horns of Negros above Dumaguete, Negros Island, Philippines (No. 571, collected by J. W. Chapman and S. F. Light on 11 May 1921 (month 5)). Plate numbers and the individual collecting records have not been translated. Hyphenated words at the ends of lines in the excerpt have been joined.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head black; abdominal tergites, the lateral areas of the sternites, the anterolateral and anterior regions of the pronotum, the basal 3 antennal segments, the anterior margins of the meso- and metanotum and the basal veins at the wing base dark brown; the middle of the pronotum, the meso- and metanotum (except the anterior margin) and the thoracic pleura pale brown; the middle area of the thoracic sternites, the legs and the terminal antennal segment yellow; wings slightly opaque yellowish brown (between Mars yellow and Sudan brown of Ridgway), the distal part of the costa opaque yellow and its base dark brown, the remaining veins thickened and darkened in the basal half of the wing and indistinct distally. Posterior part of the head rounded, longer than wide (excluding the compound eyes), its outline hidden by the very large, laterally projecting compound eyes; frons raised between the compound eyes, its sides sloping and bearing large, white, conspicuous ocelli; ocelli elongate along the long axis of the body, lemon-shaped, separated from the compound eyes by less than half their short diameter; frontal gland pore white and conspicuous, slit-shaped, almost as long as the ocelli, with radiating extensions along the transverse suture. Antennae 15-segmented, segment 1 large, cylindrical, about equal to segments 2 and 3 together, segment 3 usually slightly shorter than segment 2, segments 4—7 subequal and shorter than segment 3, segments 8—13 gradually club-shaped, segments 14 and 15 elongate-oval, segment 15 shorter and narrower than segment 14. Postclypeus very short, less than a quarter of its maximum width, inflated. Anteclypeus narrow, white; labrum pale yellow, wider than long, nearly semicircular. Head with numerous pale hairs, scattered long hairs and many short, recurved hairs. Anterior margin of the pronotum weakly concave with a slight median notch, anterolateral corners very broadly rounded, the sides rapidly narrowing to the narrow, biconvex posterior margin with a median notch; anterior margins of the meso- and metanotum weakly concave. Wing surface densely covered with minute star-shaped projections, margins with dense marginal cilia. Abdomen of the female distinctly larger than that of the male, sternite 7 very long. Measurements (mm): body length with wings 18 (male), 19—21 (female); body length 9.0 (male), 10 (female); forewing length 15.2—16.2; forewing length with wing scale 17.0; head width (including compound eyes) 1.90; head width between the compound eyes 1.08; head length 1.80; head length to the frontoclypeal suture 1.20—1.25; maximum width of the postclypeus 0.76—0.8; compound eye diameter 0.72; ocellus length 0.225; frontal gland pore length 0.16; pronotum length 0.97—1.0; pronotum width 1.8.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Body bicoloured: thorax and legs bright yellow, the rest black to blackish brown. Head black with a reddish tinge; thorax and legs bright yellow; abdominal tergites dark blackish brown; antennae dark brown, paler distally; underside of the head and mouthparts grading from brown to pale yellow; abdominal sternites pale translucent yellow, through which the opaque white fat body and the darker gut are visible. Head (Plate 6, figs. 3, 4) somewhat broadly pear-shaped, posteriorly flattened and rounded, the sides narrowing anteriorly; the posterior part of the head produced (extending far behind the neck), rounded and raised; dorsal outline of the head distinctly concave; nasus (text fig. 1, a) short, stout, conical, arising from a very broad base on the sloping frons; dorsal surface of the nasus very weakly concave, ventral surface strongly concave; with the head resting on its ventral surface the nasus forms an angle of about 40° with the horizontal; the distal third of the nasus dark red, the tip abruptly narrowed into a translucent point, surrounded by 4 (3?) forward-directed setiform hairs. Antennae (Plate 6, figs. 3, 4) long, distinctly longer than the head with the nasus; 13-segmented, segment 3 the longest, segments 2 and 13 the shortest; segment 2 slightly longer than half of segment 3; segment 4 shorter than segments 5—8, segments 5—8 subequal and slightly shorter than segment 3; segments 9—13 progressively shorter and narrower, segment 13 oval, the others club-shaped; in some specimens the base of segment 3 is inflated, as if presaging a subdivision. Mandibles (Plate 8, fig. 4) with a conspicuous yellowish brown toothless apex and a broadly rounded toothless base. Pronotum (Plate 8, fig. 1) short; the raised area low and short, bounded by a surface groove rather than by marginal notches, anterior margin entire, posterior margin with a weak median notch. Legs long (Plate 8, fig. 14), weakly hairy; mid legs longer than fore legs, hind legs much longer than both; hind tibia as long as the abdomen. Thorax almost hairless; posterior margins of the abdominal tergites with a single row of short hairs, sternites with a similar single row of long hairs and numerous short hairs; cerci conspicuous. Measurements (mm): body length 4.5—5.5; head length to the posterior margin of the antennal sockets 1.17; head width 1.20; pronotum width 0.74; pronotum length 0.38; hind femur length 1.62; hind tibia length 2.07. (The "head length with nasus" column is truncated by the OCR in the original; 1.71 is recorded in the diagnosis.)

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Two forms. Large worker: coloration as in the soldier; head elongate-oval, the sides passing indistinctly into the rounded posterior margin; sutures very distinct; frontal gland pore as in the alate, the surrounding area depressed; labrum as in Plate 7, fig. 6; postclypeus short, about three times as wide as long, inflated, anterior margin concave and posterior margin strongly convex; frons depressed behind the postclypeus; anteclypeus large, white, as long as the postclypeus. Antennae (Plate 6, fig. 7) paler and shorter than in the soldier, 14-segmented; segments 2 and 3 subequal, segment 4 the shortest; behind the antennal sockets an irregular white area, perhaps corresponding to an eyespot. Thorax slender and low; abdomen thick, arched above and flat below, humpbacked; pilosity as in the soldier but with more hairs on the head. Large worker measurements (mm): body length 5.0—5.5; head length 1.70; head length to the frontoclypeal suture 1.125; head width 1.40; pronotum width 0.864; pronotum length 0.54. Small worker: resembling the large worker but much smaller (Plate 7, figs. 5, 7); measurements (mm): head length 1.26; head length to the frontoclypeal suture 0.81; head width 1.035; pronotum width 0.65; pronotum length 0.45 (the body length column reads 8.5 in the original OCR, which contradicts 5.0—5.5 for the large worker and is probably 3.5; not altered).
